Loei is an Isan province that doesn't look like the rest of Isan, because it's full of high mountains and some of the coldest weather in the country. When people think of Loei they picture Phu Kradueng, where you climb all day to reach the top, Phu Ruea, where winter nights get cold enough to turn dew into frost, and Chiang Khan, which has become a popular riverside walking street along the Mekong. On the cultural side there's the Phi Ta Khon festival in Dan Sai, which you won't see anywhere else. For food there's down-to-earth Isan cooking plus local favourites like khai kratha and Chiang Khan's crystal coconut. Come to Loei and you can hike up a mountain, wander a Mekong town, and take some cool weather home with you.

Maha Sarakham is an education town in the heart of Isan. Two big universities fill the place with students, cafes, and budget-friendly restaurants. Around town you'll find Phra That Na Dun, considered the Buddhist center of the northeast, scattered Khmer-era ruins across several districts, and craft villages where people still do real basketry and weaving. If you want small-town Isan that's easy to get around, where food is cheap and there's history to track down, Maha Sarakham is worth a stop.
